sections.html:
Hastings is the county seat of Adams County and sits roughly 14 miles south of Interstate 80. Much of the housing goes back to the railroad years, with a second wave of building during the war years.

Downtown burned in 1879 and was rebuilt, and growth picked up again from 1900 to 1930. Those decades left Craftsman, Prairie, Colonial Revival and American Foursquare houses. Heartwell Park and Central Hastings are two of the oldest neighborhoods and are on the National Register of Historic Places. If you own in either one, ask the city whether any review applies before you plan exterior work.

sections.h2: Wartime houses and what buyers ask about them
sections.html:
The Naval Ammunition Depot, built in 1942, caused a housing shortage. The city grew from about 15,000 to 23,000 people in under a year, and existing houses were altered while new neighborhoods went up fast. An 840-unit village called Spencer Park was built for workers.

  • Houses from that push, and older ones altered to take in workers, may still have original wiring, plumbing or windows.
  • A buyer who finances may need repairs finished before the lender will fund the loan.
  • If you know the age of the house and any additions, you can fill in the disclosure form faster and leave fewer lines marked unknown.

The City of Hastings Building and Construction Inspection office covers the city limits and the extraterritorial jurisdiction. It has three inspectors, and it also staffs the Building Board of Appeals and takes complaints.

  • Contact an inspector before work that needs a permit, such as a roof tear-off, furnace swap or deck.
  • If a neighbor reports a safety concern about your structure, the same office handles it.
  • Unpermitted work tends to surface when a buyer's lender or inspector asks for records.

Ask the city what is on file for your address. If a permit was never closed out, or an addition was built without one, tell the buyer in writing before you sign. Call the office to ask whether any sale-time requirement applies to a single-family house.

sections.h2: Selling a Hastings house, step by step
sections.html:
Whether you list or take a direct offer, the paperwork follows the same order. Knowing it ahead of time keeps a closing from slipping.

  1. Pull your parcel number and last tax statement from the Adams County Treasurer in Suite 106 of the courthouse.
  2. Fill out the Nebraska seller disclosure form while the house is still free of offers, and write "unknown" where you truly do not know.
  3. Ask the city inspection office about open permits at your address.
  4. Accept an offer and give the buyer the signed disclosure no later than the effective date of the binding contract.
  5. The title company orders a title search, clears liens and prepares the deed.
  6. At closing you sign the deed. The Register of Deeds records it, and the documentary stamp tax is paid from your side of the table.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal and the loan approval, so the last three steps can move faster. The deed, the transfer statement and the recording still happen.

sections.h2: Where to record a deed and pay property tax
sections.html:
The Adams County Register of Deeds records deeds. Documents are scanned daily, so recorded papers can come back within 24 hours. The Treasurer bills real estate taxes on December 1 each year, and they are due December 31. First-half taxes become delinquent on May 1 of the next year and second-half taxes on September 1.

OfficeAddressPhone
Register of Deeds500 N. Denver Ave, Hastings402-461-7148
Treasurer500 West 4th St, Suite 106, Hastings402-461-7120

A replat is signed only after the current year's taxes are paid in full, and the Treasurer runs public and private tax sales for unpaid taxes.

The seller pays the state documentary stamp tax when the deed is recorded. For deeds recorded from July 18, 2026, it is $3.32 per $1,000 of value, up from $2.32. Confirm the current figure with the Nebraska Department of Revenue before you budget for closing, and expect the title company to collect it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: What a Hastings seller owes the buyer in writing
sections.html:
If the house has one to four units, you must hand the buyer a written disclosure statement signed by you. It has to arrive no later than the effective date of a binding purchase contract. If something on the form becomes inaccurate before then, you update it.

A seller is not liable for an error outside personal knowledge, and agents are not liable unless they knew. That is why honest answers, including "unknown," protect you. Under Nebraska Revised Statute 76-2,120, a lawsuit over a missing statement must start within one year after the buyer takes possession or the conveyance, whichever comes first.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a good fit for a Hastings house?
sections.html:
A cash sale can suit an owner when speed or condition rules out a standard listing. Older houses, estate properties and rentals with tenants often need work that a retail buyer may not want to finance.

Compare routes by what you would net. Count commissions, repairs, carrying costs such as utilities, and the taxes that accrue through December 31, then set that beside any direct offer. We do not promise a price. If you want to talk, tell us the address and what is going on with the house.

sections.h2: If property tax is still owed
sections.html:
Taxes for the year are billed December 1 and due December 31, and the first half goes delinquent May 1 of the next year. Unpaid taxes can end up in a public or private tax sale run by the Treasurer. If you owe back taxes when you sell, the title company pays them from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask for a payoff figure before you accept an offer.

Bring these to the Treasurer's office or have them ready by phone at 402-461-7120: the parcel number, your name as it appears on the deed, and the closing date you expect. If you plan to split or replat a lot before selling, remember that the replat is signed only after the current year's taxes are paid in full.

faqs.q: When are Adams County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are billed December 1 and due December 31. The first half is delinquent May 1 of the following year, and the second half is delinquent September 1.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Hastings?
faqs.a: At the Adams County Register of Deeds, 500 N. Denver Avenue in Hastings. The phone number is 402-461-7148, and recorded documents can be returned within 24 hours.

faqs.q: How much deed tax does the seller pay in Nebraska?
faqs.a: The documentary stamp tax is $3.32 for each $1,000 of value, or fraction of $1,000, for deeds recorded on or after July 18, 2026.

faqs.q: Does the city inspect a house before it sells in Hastings?
faqs.a: The Hastings inspection office serves the city and its extraterritorial area, with three inspectors. Call the office to ask whether anything applies to a single-family sale.
Hastings Public Schools serves the city. Adams Central Junior-Senior High School, a rural public school, is just outside town.
